Bug_Details:
Don't create instances of already existing BigInteger (`BigInteger.ZERO`, `BigInteger.ONE`),
for Java 1.5 onwards, BigInteger.TEN and BigDecimal (`BigDecimal.ZERO`, `BigDecimal.ONE`, `BigDecimal.TEN`) and
for Java 9 onwards `BigInteger.TWO`.
Examples:
BigInteger bi1 = new BigInteger("1");    // reference BigInteger.ONE instead
BigInteger bi2 = new BigInteger("0");    // reference BigInteger.ZERO instead
BigInteger bi3;
bi3 = new BigInteger("0");               // reference BigInteger.ZERO instead

BigDecimal bd1 = new BigDecimal(0);      // reference BigDecimal.ZERO instead
BigDecimal bd2 = new BigDecimal("0.") ;  // reference BigDecimal.ZERO instead
BigDecimal bd3 = new BigDecimal(10);     // reference BigDecimal.TEN instead
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the showBug method where new instances of BigInteger and BigDecimal are created with values that are already pre-defined by the Java standard library. This is against the best practice as it unnecessarily consumes memory.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered in the testShowBug method when the showBug method of the BigIntegerInstantiationBug class is called. This is because new instances of BigInteger and BigDecimal are created with values that are already pre-defined by the Java standard library.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results show that the test passed without any errors. This indicates that the bug was not triggered during the test run. The test code does create new instances of BigInteger and BigDecimal, but these instances are not used in a way that would cause the bug to be triggered.
